decision_triggers: If line_loss_events stays at 1 or more on the S-bend or slalom with unchanged geometry, the cause is still not geometric. Ask the Integrator to inspect the line_loss handling and the start pose before any geometry edit.
If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, test wheel_track 0.12 m for more differential turn authority, as the feedback suggests.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
integration_questions: At what course position does the S-bend and slalom line loss begin, and what are the sensor readings and signal at that moment?
Does last_direction or a search direction change the S-bend and slalom loss count, with geometry held fixed?
Does the 0.6 kg mass reduce steering oscillation or max_error compared with 0.7 kg at the same gains? The iteration 4 data suggests little effect.

intent: Hold the iteration 4 geometry unchanged so the S-bend and slalom line losses can be attributed to the controller and start position rather than to the body. Test whether the controller's line_loss handling (last_direction or a search direction) and the start alignment clear the S-bend and slalom losses. Geometry changes (wheel_track 0.12 m for turn authority, or wheel_radius 0.035 m for speed) remain queued and are only triggered by the rules in the Robot Integrator feedback.
learning: Iterations 3 and 4 show the outer span at plus or minus 0.05 m clears the oval line loss but not the S-bend or slalom loss, and mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg has negligible effect on progress or max_error. Geometry looks close to its limit for these tracks. Record whether the controller-side change clears the S-bend and slalom losses, and revise the geometry hypotheses only if it does not.
rationale: Iteration 4 (mass 0.6 kg, otherwise identical to iteration 3) scored 54.98, slightly below iteration 3's 55.27. The oval line loss stayed at 0 and max_error stayed at about 0.063 m, which is still above the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit. The S-bend (0.95 events) and slalom (1.0 event) still lose the line, and progress did not improve on either track (0.16 and 0.11). Lowering mass therefore did not reduce bend overshoot in any measurable way. Body width cannot move the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) stays at 0.06 m), and the span at plus or minus 0.05 m already removed the oval loss, so geometry has no further lever that the evidence supports. The S-bend and slalom losses persist with the span and footprint that clear the oval, which points to the controller's line-loss handling or the start position rather than the geometry. Following the feedback rule that applies when line loss persists at 0.6 kg, I make no geometry change this iteration. I keep mass at 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 by 0.12 m, sensors at plus or minus 0.05 m, 16 mm footprints and y = 0.04 m, so the Integrator's controller work is the only variable that changes. Expected result: the score stays near 55 unless the controller clears the S-bend and slalom losses, in which case progress should rise sharply on those tracks.
